To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deposition of cellulose micro-fibrils (CMF) in cortical cells of freshly cut tobacco explants occurs in two alternating directions, at approximately 75° and at 115° with respect to the long axis of the cell.
the microtubule cytoskeleton is not required for cellulose microfibration deposition, and that changes in the deposition of cellulose microtibrils are controlled by cell polarity factors.

in the cell walls of cortical cells of tobacco flower stalk explants, microtubules are not required for cellulose microfbril (CMF) deposition and the orientation of the CMFs is determined by factors related to the cell polarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the orientation of the cellulose microfbrils is determined in the walls of plant cells.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deposition of cellulose micro fibrils (CMFs), which are the main structural elements in plant cell wall, is a dynamic process in plant cells, which is controlled by the polarity of the cell.
the orientation of microfibril deposition is not controlled by microtubules, but by cell polarity, which is not controlled by the microtubule array.
the deposition of cellulose microfibils in the walls of tobacco explant cortical cells is controlled by a mechanism which is not microtubule dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the orientation of cellulose micro fibrils is controlled by the orientation of microtubules.
the orientation of microtubules is determined by factors related to the polarity of cells, whereas the orientation of cellulose microfibils is determined by the orientation of microfibrils.

the microtubules in cortical cells of Nicotiana explants are oriented randomly in the first 6 h after explantation and that the microturbules become oriented parallel to the longitudinal axis after 6 h.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microtubule cytoskeleton in plant cells may not control cellulose microfibration orientation in the cell wall.
microtubule reorientation in plant cells is not a passive process, but is actively driven.
the microtubule cytoskeleton is not the only factor involved in controlling the orientation of CMF deposition in plant cells, and that cell polarity is a key player.
